key_insight: Stacking ensemble learning produced the most accurate predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while the multitask neural network offered strong shared-learning performance across related welding targets.
engineering_relevance: The results help welding engineers choose between a single shared model for related outputs and task-specific ensembles when precise prediction of weld quality and mechanical properties is the priority.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers with task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Predicted three welding response variables: UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness.
Evaluated performance using RMSE and R² across the shared dataset.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved lower RMSE and higher R² than MTNN for all three outputs, with especially strong gains for UTS and weld hardness.
watch_item: Model performance is reported on one shared dataset, so generalization to other welding processes, materials, or unseen parameter ranges should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
